findings.claim: Every single L4 Inputs row in the workflow names the upstream stage's `output/README.md` — the authored *declaration* — instead of the artifact that stage declares. record-shapes.md §1a rule 3 requires an L4 input to "name a file some earlier stage's `output/` declares"; `README.md` is not declared by anything, it is the declaring file. The real contract-bearing artifacts (`contract.md`, `behavior-units.ndjson`, `behavior-units.normalized.ndjson`, `classifications.ndjson`, `candidates.md`, `draft-report.md`, `lint-report.md`, `findings.ndjson`) appear in NO Inputs table anywhere in the workflow, which is also a convention.md §1a rule 1 completeness violation on ~20 rows.
findings.evidence: 10-inventory Inputs row is `../00-contract/output/README.md | L4 | upstream artifact produced by 00-contract — subject repository, pinned revision, scope, and exclusions` while its own body says "per `contract.md`" and "restricted to `contract.md`'s scope and exclusions". 30-normalize inputs `../20-harvest/output/README.md` but its How-to-do-it says "Go through `../20-harvest/output/behavior-units.ndjson` in order". 40-classify inputs `../30-normalize/output/README.md` but its durable outcome is "every unit from `../30-normalize/output/behavior-units.normalized.ndjson`". The Why-column text describes the artifact, not the README, in all cases. validate-structure.py S4 does not catch this: its L4 branch only requires `parts[1] == "output"` and an earlier source stage (lines 280–295), and it was explicitly written to tolerate a not-yet-existing artifact filename ("names an artifact that doesn't exist yet (expected, per-run)") — so the correct form was available and was not used. Consequence for a stranger executing 30-normalize: the pinned Inputs table hands them a README that says "This directory is empty in the authored tree", not the corpus they must rewrite.

findings.claim: Four stages omit contract-bearing dependencies that their own pinned L3 reference material requires them to open — convention.md §1a rule 1 / record-shapes.md §1a rule 4 ("a contract-bearing dependency missing from the table is a violation"). These are omissions of whole rows, distinct from C1's wrong-path problem.
findings.evidence: 80-adversarial-review Inputs lists 00/40/60/70 only, but `references/challenge-checklist.md` (an Input, therefore contract) directs it to sample `../30-normalize/output/behavior-units.normalized.ndjson` (Axis 2, "Re-verify a sample of citations"), to read `../50-synthesize/output/candidates.md` (Axis 2, "Hidden translation"), and to use `../_config/evidence-policy.md` and `../_config/icm-ladder.md` §6.3/6.1–6.6 (Axes 2 and 3) — none are rows. 70-lint Inputs lists only `references/mechanical-vs-substantive.md` and `../60-draft/output/README.md`, but that reference file requires consulting `../40-classify/output/classifications.ndjson` to decide whether a missing `engine_gap` field is mechanical. 50-synthesize's `references/synthesis-method.md` bucket 6 and 7 direct it to `../_config/icm-ladder.md`, absent from its Inputs. 90-reconcile's `references/reconciliation-method.md` §3 requires `../_config/icm-ladder.md` §6.7's six-field template, absent from its Inputs. A fresh per-stage agent given only the pinned context cannot reach any of these.

findings.claim: The root catalog does not exist, while `repo-to-icm` declares `status: published` and lives under `.sergeant/workflows/`. convention.md §1 rule 1: the root index "MUST list every admitted workflow… A published workflow absent from the root index is a violation"; record-shapes.md §1 rule 2 repeats it. The workflow's own validator does not check for it, so the N2 gate condition "it must itself pass reference-corpus-grade lint (the validator runs on its own tree)" is satisfied by a PASS that steps over a documented violation.
findings.evidence: `ls .sergeant/` returns only `workflows/` — no `index.md`, no `common/`. `python3 .sergeant/workflows/repo-to-icm/scripts/validate-structure.py` prints "PASS: structure is clean", exit 0. validate-structure.py's check list S1–S10 contains no catalog check; `check_no_misplaced_drafts` only compares front-matter `status` against location.

findings.claim: 70-lint's validator invocation does not match what validate-structure.py checks: the validator implements neither of the two checks convention.md §1a (D9) explicitly names as structurally lintable — "disposition present; finalize step present when outputs are declared" — yet 70-lint's own reference material triages a defect class the validator can never emit.
findings.evidence: `grep -in 'disposition|finalize' scripts/validate-structure.py` returns nothing; the S1–S10 list has no disposition or finalize check. Meanwhile 70-lint/references/mechanical-vs-substantive.md lists under Mechanical: "A missing `**Disposition:**` line in a candidate's own stage `output/README.md` where the artifact description already makes the intended disposition unambiguous" and under Substantive: "A missing `**Disposition:**` line where the artifact's own purpose is NOT obvious". Nothing in the run surfaces that defect, so a generated candidate whose stage output/README.md declares no disposition passes 70-lint clean — and then that candidate, if promoted and run, will make its own finalize.py-equivalent fail closed. The convention's claim that both halves of D9 are lintable is unimplemented in the very validator N2 designates as the §9.7 structural validator.

findings.claim: The run's central safety constraint is stage instruction parked in Layer 1, and is therefore unreachable by 5 of the 10 stages. convention.md §1a rule 5: Layer 1 "MUST NOT contain stage instructions", the engine does not deliver it, and stages that need it must name it in their Inputs table. The blindness rule is imperative stage instruction ("never open it, never grep it", "A stage that needs to check its own output's shape uses `scripts/validate-structure.py`, never `reference-corpus/lint.py`"), so Layer 1 is being used as a super-stage; and no stage except `00-contract` lists `../CONTEXT.md`.
findings.evidence: `grep -rln reference-corpus */CONTEXT.md CONTEXT.md` matches only `CONTEXT.md`, `80-adversarial-review/CONTEXT.md`, `90-reconcile/CONTEXT.md`. Stages 30-normalize, 40-classify, 50-synthesize, 60-draft, 70-lint list neither `../CONTEXT.md` (L1) nor any 00-contract row, so a fresh agent running 40-classify with only its pinned context has no statement of the blindness rule and no exclusion record. That 80 and 90 restate the rule inline shows the author knew L1 does not travel — the fix was applied to two stages, not the other five. This is exactly the N2 contract Outcome §2 requirement ("blind… enforced by prompt") and it is enforced by prompt in half the pipeline.

findings.claim: 70-lint's invocation guarantees the engine-gap lint never runs in a real run. record-shapes.md §5 rule 1 and _config/icm-ladder.md both state an incomplete engine-gap claim "is auto-rejected at lint, never merely flagged for review" — but S9 walks only the tree it is pointed at, and 70-lint points it exclusively at candidate packages while explicitly declining the no-argument mode that would cover where the records actually live.
findings.evidence: S9 (`check_engine_gap_records`, line 335) walks `pkg_dir`. 70-lint step 1: "Run `python3 ../scripts/validate-structure.py <candidate-path>`" — draft mode, candidate tree only. Engine-gap records are produced into `40-classify/output/classifications.ndjson` and `90-reconcile/output/grammar-pressure.ndjson`, both inside repo-to-icm's own tree, never inside a candidate package (60-draft's contract: engine-pressure candidates "are **not** materialized as packages"). 70-lint's Purpose then rules out the only invocation that would reach them: "This stage's own tree (`repo-to-icm` itself) is expected to already pass the same validator run with no arguments — that is a property of how this workflow was authored, not something this stage needs to re-verify at run time." That statement is true of the authored tree and false of a run worktree, where 40-classify has just written new NDJSON into it. Confirmed empirically: the no-arg run reports "engine-gap records checked: 0".

findings.claim: The helper invocations are cwd-relative and unexecutable as written by the fresh stranger agent the workflow is designed for. Nothing in any stage context establishes a working directory, and the helper is not named in any Inputs table, so the path has no anchor.
findings.evidence: 70-lint: "Run `python3 ../scripts/validate-structure.py <candidate-path>`". 90-reconcile: "Run `python3 ../scripts/finalize.py` (no argument…)". `../scripts/` resolves correctly only from inside the stage directory; from a worktree root — the normal cwd for an agent handed a work surface — it escapes the repository entirely. `<candidate-path>` is likewise unanchored (60-draft's manifest records paths, but relative to what is never stated). Neither helper appears as an Inputs row in the stage that runs it, so there is no declared path a stranger can fall back on. Contrast the workflow-relative form used everywhere else in the same files (`.sergeant/drafts/workflows/<candidate-name>/`).

findings.claim: The workflow's principal deliverable — the materialized draft packages — is per-run Layer 4 content written outside any stage's `output/`, carries no disposition anywhere, and is deliberately excluded from finalize. convention.md §1a rule 2 puts run-produced content in Layer 4; the D9 working rule says "every declared output carries a disposition" and that finalize "applies the policy mechanically: keep `promote` files, remove `evidence`-class and undeclared files". The draft packages satisfy neither half, and the workflow asserts this is fine rather than recording it as the D9/U3 pressure it is.
findings.evidence: 60-draft/CONTEXT.md "Output": "the *materialized packages themselves* live under `.sergeant/drafts/workflows/`, outside this stage's own `output/` directory". 60-draft/output/README.md: "`../scripts/finalize.py` does not touch them". finalize.py's docstring: "This script does NOT touch a generated draft workflow package's own `output/` directories" — but its `find_stage_dirs`/`plan_stage` also never see the packages themselves, which are not under any stage directory at all. The justification given ("they are per-run artifact declarations for that *candidate's future runs*") is true of the candidates' empty `output/README.md` files and false of the packages, which are unambiguously produced by this run. Net effect: the one output N2 exists to produce is the only output D9's mechanism does not govern, and the workflow's grammar-pressure report has no instruction to record that.

findings.claim: Broken cross-reference in pinned L3 material: it names an artifact filename that no stage declares. The hedge "(or equivalent)" pushes a resolution decision onto the actor that the Inputs/declaration convention exists to remove.
findings.evidence: challenge-checklist.md Axis 1: "Every candidate package named in `../60-draft/output/manifest.md` (or equivalent)". 60-draft/output/README.md declares `draft-report.md`, and 80's own Inputs row and 70-lint both use `draft-report.md`. `grep -rn 'manifest.md' .` returns exactly this one hit. Not caught by the validator, whose S4 path resolution covers Inputs-table rows only, never prose paths in `references/`.

findings.claim: S5's `@@name` resolution check covers only each stage's `CONTEXT.md`, so convention.md §4 is unenforced in `_config/`, `references/`, and `common/contexts/` — and, in the other direction, it cannot distinguish a mention of the token from a use of it. The workflow's own text works around the check rather than fixing it.
findings.evidence: `AT_NAME_RE.findall(text)` at line 303 runs inside `check_inputs_table`, whose `text` is the stage CONTEXT.md only. The tree itself demonstrates the gap: literal `@@name` tokens sit unchecked in `60-draft/references/draft-package-template.md:81,85` and `90-reconcile/references/reconciliation-method.md:85`, and the validator still reports PASS with no `.sergeant/common/contexts/` directory in existence. Conversely 60-draft/CONTEXT.md step 5 has to write "the shared-context include token (two `@` characters followed by a name)" instead of the token, purely to avoid tripping S5 on a mention — the periphrasis is evidence the check is misplaced, and it makes the draft-boundary instruction harder for a stranger to follow than the reference file that states it plainly.

findings.claim: Independent of C1's path problem, tagging `output/README.md` rows `L4` mislabels the layer. convention.md §1a rule 2: "The layer split is lifetime, not distance. A file belongs in Layer 3 iff it does not change between runs". Each `output/README.md` is authored, committed, and identical across every run — it is Layer-3-lifetime content that happens to live at a Layer-4 address.
findings.evidence: Every `output/README.md` in the tree opens "Layer 4 (per-run artifact)… This directory is empty in the authored tree", describing the directory's future contents, not itself. The files are static authored declarations, per convention.md §1a rule 4 ("An `output/` directory in the authored tree contains only a `README.md`… declaring the expected artifacts"). validate-structure.py reinforces the confusion by deriving the layer from the path shape (`parts[1] == "output"` ⇒ L4) rather than from lifetime.

findings.claim: A second invocation/checks mismatch: the validator always runs one repo-wide check regardless of the target, so 70-lint's per-candidate report has nowhere to file the defects it can produce.
findings.evidence: `main()` calls `check_no_misplaced_drafts(lint, repo_root)` on every invocation, unconditionally, and its S7 failures are keyed by an arbitrary package name ("`{name}`: index.md declares `status: …` while living under …"). 70-lint's durable outcome requires recording findings "under that candidate's own heading" and "covering every candidate package named in `../60-draft/output/draft-report.md`" — an S7 hit against an unrelated package satisfies neither, and the stage is given no instruction for it. Also unattributable: repeated across N candidate invocations, the same repo-wide defect is reported N times.

findings.claim: `version` is a quoted string in workflow.toml and an integer in index.md; record-shapes.md §1 requires "a monotonically increasing integer". The validator checks neither the type nor the agreement between the two files, so the divergence it would be reasonable to expect S1 to catch passes silently — and 60-draft's template propagates the string form into every generated candidate.
findings.evidence: workflow.toml: `version = "1"`. index.md front matter: `version: 1`. check_front_matter only tests presence/non-emptiness of `version` (line 148) and check_workflow_toml only compares `name` (line 193). 60-draft/references/draft-package-template.md prescribes `workflow.toml  [workflow] name = "<candidate-name>", version = "1"` — the string form, for every candidate.

findings.claim: The finalize ordering leaves the run's closing commit incomplete and the worktree dirty, undercutting D9's "executed rather than reviewed… in a final commit".
findings.evidence: Step 4: "Run `python3 ../scripts/finalize.py`… Record its full output at the end of `output/measurement-package.md`." finalize.py performs `git rm` plus `git commit` (lines 274–287) and returns; the actor then edits `measurement-package.md`, a file finalize just committed as `promote`. The result is a modified-after-finalize tracked file with no instruction to commit it, so the "final commit" is not final and `measurement-package.md`'s recorded finalize output is not in the history finalize created.

findings.claim: convention.md §4 fixes `@@name` resolution "by `AGENTS.md`, per §3", and §3 gives AGENTS.md as the surface that teaches a harness to resolve these conventions. Neither AGENTS.md nor `.sergeant/common/` exists, so the resolution rule the workflow repeatedly cites has no anchor in this repository, and 60-draft's instruction to only use `@@` when it "resolves to a real, already-existing `.sergeant/common/contexts/<name>.md`" is unconditionally unsatisfiable for every candidate this workflow will ever generate.
findings.evidence: `ls AGENTS.md` → No such file; `ls .sergeant/` → `workflows/` only. 60-draft/references/draft-package-template.md nevertheless instructs "this stage does not create new files under `.sergeant/common/` itself (that is a promotion-time decision for a human)", making shared-context representation (`shared-context`, ladder §6.6, a live output of 40-classify and bucket 5 of 50-synthesize) structurally unreachable in draft output. Worth flagging because §6.6 is one of the rungs the run is measured on.

findings.claim: The blindness rule is invisible to seven of the ten stages. Only `00-contract` names `../CONTEXT.md` in its Inputs table, and only `80`/`90` restate blindness in their own contracts. Stages 10–70 — including the two contamination-critical ones, `10-inventory` (enumerates every file in scope) and `20-harvest` (mints citations) — receive no instruction not to read `reference-corpus/`.
findings.evidence: `grep -ci blind */CONTEXT.md` → 00:0, 10:0, 20:0, 30:0, 40:0, 50:0, 60:0, 70:0, 80:4, 90:2. The rule lives only in `CONTEXT.md` L20-43, and workflow `CONTEXT.md` itself states 'only the first stage lists this file in its Inputs table (§1a rule 5)'. A fresh `20-harvest` agent given exactly its pinned context (`00-contract/output/README.md`, `10-inventory/output/README.md`, `_config/evidence-policy.md`, `references/extraction-example.md`) has literally no text telling it the answer key exists or is off-limits; its only guard is whatever `00-contract` happened to write into `contract.md`.

findings.claim: The prescribed method for pinning the subject revision produces the wrong SHA, and the resulting pin is unusable by `10-inventory`. `reference/sergeant-upstream` is a vendored subtree with no `.git` of its own, and the frozen SHA is not an object in this repository.
findings.evidence: `git -C reference/sergeant-upstream rev-parse HEAD` → `5d03f8b3e410d2482cc166ecdb3bedefc02fb012` (the *outer* sergeant-rs HEAD, which moves every commit), not the frozen `f430cfd4f90174a98adbd7abebbece6303817929`. `git cat-file -t f430cfd4…` → `fatal: could not get object info`. So `00-contract`'s 'resolve `HEAD` of the named subject and record the resulting SHA' yields a value that is not the frozen reference point N2 requires, and `10-inventory` step 1's '`git ls-files`, run against the pinned SHA' cannot execute against either value. The frozen SHA is discoverable only from `reference/UPSTREAM.md` or `reference-corpus/FROZEN.md` — the latter is blind, and neither is named in any stage's context.

findings.claim: The blindness check is specified to produce guaranteed false positives at highest severity. It greps generated artifacts for the literal string `reference-corpus` and instructs the actor to treat any hit as contamination without reading the match — but `00-contract` is explicitly instructed to write that directory's name into `contract.md`.
findings.evidence: Checklist: 'grep the *generated* artifacts for the literal string `reference-corpus`… Any hit is a contamination finding and should be marked highest severity… you do not need to read the target of a match to know it is a boundary violation.' Against `00-contract/CONTEXT.md` L36-40: 'If the Work's task identifies such a directory, exclude it explicitly and name it in `contract.md`.' A correctly-executed `00-contract` therefore makes a correctly-executed `80` emit a top-severity contamination finding about a legitimate exclusion record. The checklist gives no rule distinguishing a *citation* into the corpus (`source.path`) from a *policy mention* of it.

findings.target: All ten stage CONTEXT.md Inputs tables (L4 rows)
findings.claim: Every L4 Inputs row names the upstream stage's authored `output/README.md` — the artifact *declaration* — rather than the artifact itself, so the declared dependency set of every stage resolves to no data. This also fails `record-shapes.md` §1a rule 3 ('An L4 input MUST name a file some earlier stage's `output/` declares'): `README.md` is the declarer, not a declared file.
findings.evidence: e.g. `10-inventory/CONTEXT.md`: `| ../00-contract/output/README.md | L4 | upstream artifact produced by `00-contract` — subject repository, pinned revision, scope, and exclusions this stage enumerates within |` — but that content lives in `contract.md`. `90-reconcile` lists nine such rows and its body then says 'pulling stats from every upstream stage's output named in the Inputs table above', which names nine READMEs and zero artifacts. Worst case for a stranger: `10-inventory` and `20-harvest` bodies never state the real paths (`../00-contract/output/contract.md`, `../10-inventory/output/inventory.md`) anywhere, so the filename is recoverable only by a second hop into the README.

findings.claim: Four contract-bearing dependencies are missing from `80-adversarial-review`'s Inputs table, all of them required by the very checklist the table does declare — a `convention.md` §1a rule 1 violation and an executability gap for a fresh agent that loads only declared inputs.
findings.evidence: `references/challenge-checklist.md` requires reading `../30-normalize/output/behavior-units.normalized.ndjson` (Axis 2 citation re-verification), `../50-synthesize/output/candidates.md` (Axis 2 hidden-translation), `../_config/icm-ladder.md` (Axis 2 reimplementation test, Axis 3 rung re-attempt), and `../_config/evidence-policy.md` (the `printf '%s' "$QUOTE" | sha256sum` procedure). The Inputs table lists only `references/challenge-checklist.md`, `../00-contract/output/README.md`, `../40-classify/…`, `../60-draft/…`, `../70-lint/…`. Same class of omission at `70-lint` (its `mechanical-vs-substantive.md` requires `../40-classify/output/classifications.ndjson`, undeclared) and `90-reconcile` (must write six-field records whose template is in `../_config/icm-ladder.md`, undeclared).

findings.claim: The quote+hash procedure is under-specified in exactly the two ways that make harvest and review disagree mechanically: it never says whether the hash covers the *raw file bytes* or the *JSON-escaped* string, and it never reconciles line-range extraction (which includes a trailing newline) with the `printf '%s'` recipe (which does not).
findings.evidence: Policy says 'hash the literal bytes you are about to put in `quote`' — but the bytes 'put in quote' are JSON-escaped (`\n`), while the rule elsewhere says 'the exact contiguous byte span quoted from the cited file — no normalization'. It then recommends 'If you quoted a byte range from the file directly (recommended over retyping), hash that extracted range' with no command; the natural `sed -n '3,5p' f | sha256sum` appends a newline the example's `quote` value lacks. `80-adversarial-review` verifies with `printf '%s' "$QUOTE" | sha256sum`. A harvester who follows the recommended path and a reviewer who follows the verification path get different digests, and every such unit is recorded as 'invention' per checklist Axis 2 — corrupting the measurement the run exists to produce. The only worked example (`extraction-example.md`) sidesteps this by writing the placeholder `sha256:<hex of the exact span above>` instead of a real digest.

findings.claim: `90-reconcile`'s declared outcome — 'reports the internally-computable §9.9 dimensions' — is not achievable from its pinned context, and the method's own stat list silently drops two of the five dimensions it implies are covered.
findings.evidence: Proposal §9.9's ten dimensions are: source coverage, behavioral recall, behavioral precision, workflow-boundary agreement, stage-boundary agreement, representation agreement, engine-gap quality, provenance completeness, draft validity, review convergence. The method names five as out of reach (recall, workflow-boundary, stage-boundary, representation agreement, engine-gap quality), implying five are covered — but its prescribed block lists 'run identity, source coverage, extraction coverage, normalization outcome, representation mix, candidate yield, draft materialization, draft validity, review convergence', omitting **behavioral precision** and **provenance completeness** (both internally computable) and substituting non-§9.9 labels ('representation mix' is not 'representation agreement'). The proposal itself is never named by path in any stage context, so a fresh agent cannot recover the dimension names to check its own coverage.

findings.claim: `finalize.py` will exit 2 for a stranger who followed the stage instructions, because nothing tells the actor to `git add` its outputs first — and if it does succeed, its bare `git commit` sweeps the whole index, and the ordering it prescribes leaves the finalize record uncommitted.
findings.evidence: finalize.py runs `git rm -f -- <paths>`, which fails on untracked files; `90-reconcile` only says 'only after 1–3 are complete and committed to their output files' ('committed to' as prose, not `git commit`). The commit call passes no pathspec, so any unrelated staged change in the run worktree is folded into the D9 finalize commit. And step 4 orders 'run finalize, then record its output verbatim at the end of `output/measurement-package.md`' — finalize has already made the closing commit, so the recorded output lands in a dirty tree after the run's declared closing act.

findings.claim: 'The six buckets' is a heading over seven numbered buckets, `helper` has no bucket keyed by its own `representation` value, and the exactly-one-appearance reconciliation rule only covers buckets 1–3 — so the stage's completeness criterion cannot be checked deterministically.
findings.evidence: Heading 'The six buckets' followed by items 1–7 (workflow, stage, stage-context, permanent-instruction, shared helper/context, obsolete-mechanism, engine-pressure). The opening rule is 'Every classification record … lands in exactly one of these buckets, **by its `representation` field**', but `representation: helper` matches no bucket's keying — it is only swept up by bucket 1's parenthetical 'plus the `stage`/`stage-context`/`helper` records whose `workflow` field names the same candidate', which fails for a `helper` record with no `workflow` value. 'What must not happen' then defines the appearance rule only for 'buckets 1–3'. `CONTEXT.md` L23 and `output/README.md` L8 both repeat 'six buckets'.

findings.claim: `grammar-pressure.ndjson` — a named N2 deliverable — has no record-shape specification. Unlike `findings.ndjson` (which carries a literal JSON example), the actor is told only 'a full six-field record … tagged `"source": "behavior"` with the originating `behavior_id`', leaving the wrapper shape to invention.
findings.evidence: `80-adversarial-review/CONTEXT.md` L73-74 gives `{"id": "AF-0001", "axis": …}` verbatim; `90-reconcile` gives nothing equivalent. Unresolved by the text: whether the six fields are flattened at top level or nested under `engine_gap`; whether `representation: engine-gap` is carried (if it is, `validate-structure.py` S9 — which walks *any* `.ndjson` under the tree — will demand a nested `engine_gap` object and fail the workflow's own tree); whether `behavior_id`/`stage` are fields or prose; and what a `source: meta` record uses in place of `source_evidence` (there is no behavior unit behind a meta-level gap).

findings.claim: 'Stop here and ask' is prescribed as the fail-closed path for the first stage, but no mechanism for asking is named, and the engine this workflow is contracted to run on has no actor-initiated input request. A fresh agent hitting the ambiguity has no executable next move and will either guess (the outcome the rule forbids) or stall the run.
findings.evidence: '**Fail closed, not by guessing.** If the subject repository, its revision, or the scope is ambiguous after reading the Work's task and this worktree, stop here and ask rather than picking a plausible default.' Nothing in the stage context, `../CONTEXT.md`, or `_config/` names a surface for this (no `sgt respond`/`needs_input` reference); `docs/gauntlet/contracts/N2.md` U1 flags fake-backend hold-open semantics as unmeasured. Given F2, revision ambiguity is the *expected* case for the N2 run, so this path will be taken.

findings.claim: The checklist names a nonexistent artifact: `../60-draft/output/manifest.md`. The declared artifact is `draft-report.md`.
findings.evidence: Checklist Axis 1: 'Every candidate package named in `../60-draft/output/manifest.md` (or equivalent)'. `60-draft/output/README.md` L8 and `70-lint/CONTEXT.md` L31 both name `draft-report.md`. The '(or equivalent)' hedge asks a fresh agent to guess rather than resolve, and `80`'s Inputs row points at `60-draft/output/README.md`, whose text does give the right name — so the two authored sources disagree in the same stage's pinned context.

findings.claim: Helper invocations are written as stage-relative paths (`python3 ../scripts/validate-structure.py`) with no statement of the actor's working directory, and the helpers are absent from both stages' Inputs tables.
findings.evidence: `../scripts/validate-structure.py` resolves only if cwd is the stage directory. A fresh agent in a materialized work surface ordinarily starts at the worktree root, where the command is `python3 .sergeant/workflows/repo-to-icm/scripts/validate-structure.py`. Neither `70-lint` nor `90-reconcile` declares its helper in the Inputs table, and no stage context states the cwd convention. (Both scripts do resolve their own workflow root from `__file__`, so only the invocation path is at risk — but that is the part the actor types.)

findings.claim: `60-draft`'s and `80`'s collision checks reference two paths that do not exist in the worktree, and the catalog file the convention makes mandatory is missing — leaving a stranger to decide silently whether to create them.
findings.evidence: `ls .sergeant/` → `workflows` only. `convention.md` §1 rule 1: '`.sergeant/index.md` is the root catalog. It MUST list every admitted workflow' — `repo-to-icm` is admitted and there is no root index (and `validate-structure.py` does not check for one, so `70-lint` will not catch it either). `60-draft/CONTEXT.md` L38-41 and `draft-package-template.md` L16-18 instruct 're-check every candidate name against `.sergeant/workflows/`, `.sergeant/drafts/workflows/`' — the latter does not exist; nothing says whether `60-draft` creates it or treats its absence as an error.
